fr.elements: Main Building; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Road; Internal Drive Aisle; Landscaped Area; Detached Building; Walkway; Open Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the single access point with a clearly visible address sign readable from both directions of approach.
• Post the building address at the access road entry so responding units can confirm the correct property without entering.
• Mark the internal drive aisle with directional arrows to guide responding units toward the main building and detached building without hesitation.
• Identify a designated staging area within the vehicle parking area and mark it to keep it clear for emergency vehicles during an incident.
• Trim dense vegetation along the access road to maintain clear sightlines and prevent vegetation from obscuring the roadway edge or overhead clearance for larger emergency vehicles.
• Mark the detached building with a visible identifier so responding units can distinguish it from the main building on arrival.
• Keep the walkway connections between the main building and detached building clear to allow responder movement between structures.
• Post a site map at the access point showing the locations of the main building, detached building, drive aisle, and any areas where rear access is restricted.
• Identify and mark any secondary access points to the rear of the property, or clearly indicate to arriving units that rear access is not available from the primary approach.

wildfire.conditions: Large Paved Area; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Building; Scattered Shrubs; Open Paved Area; Limited Rear Access; Multiple Access Routes
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches from trees in the cluster that hang over or within a few feet of any building roofline or wall.
• Remove shrubs and low vegetation growing directly against building walls and foundations.
• Thin the tree cluster by removing dead wood and lower branches to reduce the amount of combustible material concentrated in one area.
• Keep the large paved area and open paved surfaces clear of fallen leaves, dead plant debris, and any vegetation encroachment along the edges.
• Cut back scattered shrubs that have grown close to building entrances, windows, or vents.
• Trim lower branches from scattered trees near buildings so flames cannot travel from ground vegetation up into the tree canopy.
• Clear any vegetation, debris, or stored materials from the rear of the building to improve access for emergency crews working in that area.
• Keep all access routes and drive lanes clear of overhanging branches, encroaching shrubs, and surface debris so vehicles can move without obstruction.
• Maintain the open paved areas between vegetation and buildings by keeping them free of plant material, mulch piles, or stored combustibles.
